correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the published tight-chain high-energy condition and at \(A=1/4\) reduces it exactly to the periodic sign condition \(-\cos((2m+1)x)\sin(mx)\sin((m+1)x)\ge0\). On \(0<t<1\), the sign changes of the two sine factors interlace explicitly, while those of the cosine form a uniform half-step grid. Pairing the jumps yields an exact mismatch length; the two parity cases give \(P_m=3/4-[4(2m+1)s_m]^{-1}\). The source’s symmetric-chain formula gives \(P=1/2\) at quarter flux. Exact Fraction arithmetic independently checks the measure identity for \(1\le m\le200\), and dense midpoint sampling checks representative cases. The only limiting passage is from the source’s asymptotic band criterion to density; finite zero sets per period and uniform smallness of the remainder away from them make the density argument valid.

originality.rationale: The primary magnetic-ring-chain paper explicitly treats rational arc ratios as nonuniversal and says their probabilities are obtained numerically rather than in closed form, while giving closed forms only for the incommensurate and exactly symmetric cases. The present all-\(m\) adjacent-ratio formula and the resulting discontinuity are not stated there. Searches for the exact ratio family, quarter-flux formula, commensurate band density, and the equivalent trigonometric sign-measure formulation returned no covering result; the closest broad theorem concerns generic edge lengths and therefore does not imply the rational formula.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural commensurate family left numerical in the source and quantifies the arithmetic failure of generic universality with an exact \(m^{-2}\) correction. The limiting geometry approaches the symmetric chain while the band density approaches the incommensurate maximum \(3/4\), whereas the symmetric value is \(1/2\). This is a structural boundary phenomenon in the source’s central spectral-density observable rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
